headline: Cerebras chief executive Andrew Feldman says a shortage of data centres at his company was a key reason OpenAI turned to Nvidia chips for its next-generation models.
score_reason: Lowered by 1 from 6: Feldman spoke on 13 Oct 2026, and the explanation is his own.
importance_line: It affects Cerebras investors and AI buyers choosing chips, and the explanation comes from Cerebras itself, not from OpenAI.
summary: digitimes reports that Andrew Feldman, co-founder and chief executive of Cerebras Systems, which makes very large single-chip AI processors, said at TechCrunch Disrupt on 13 Oct 2026 that a shortage of data-centre capacity was a key reason OpenAI turned to Nvidia GPUs for its next-generation models. BigGo Finance adds that Cerebras shares fell about 19.5% between 25 Sep and 2 Oct, and that OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said on 2 Oct that Cerebras is "a close partner".
notes: Share-price and Altman details from BigGo Finance.
